bug_semantics: Budibase automation actions accepted an automation-supplied URL and made a server-side HTTP request without applying the outbound IP blacklist. This allowed an automation author to target loopback, private-network, link-local/cloud-metadata, or other internal services. The related REST datasource check was also opt-in because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list. A first automation patch checked only the initial URL, so node-fetch's automatic redirects could still reach a blacklisted address; the closing patch manually followed redirects and checked every destination.
flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first added the OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation action and its run function, taking inputs.url and passing it to server-side axios with no address policy. The immediate parent has neither the file nor an outgoing-webhook request path. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb merely replaced axios with node-fetch and is not the BIC; later Slack, Zapier, Discord, Make, and n8n actions replicated the already-existing flaw.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3` shows author and committer `mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>` and only the message `Adding an outgoing webhook action, so that we have both incoming and outgoing ability.`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI attribution trailer.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git log -L '/module.exports.run = async function/,+45':packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js 3d771637...` reaches 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 and shows that commit adding the complete run function with `let { requestMethod, url, requestBody } = inputs` and `await axios(request)`; the next commit 3d771637... only changes that call to `fetch(url, request)`. `git log --follow -S'const response = await axios(request)' -- .../outgoingWebhook.js` likewise returns addition in 3ae82b95... and removal in 3d771637.... `git cat-file -e 3ae82b95^:packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js` fails, and `git grep -E 'OUTGOING_WEBHOOK|Outgoing webhook|axios\(request\)|fetch\(url' 3ae82b95^ -- packages/server/src/automations` has no match; `git show -s --format=%P 3ae82b95...` gives f9eeefb4dca55aec17f2e5088ac483cdcd257b95. The BIC is a focused, one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate. For the fix lifecycle, 62f50d9779cbd7673bc5b1d99e167f3d2e175ec1 adds hardcoded private/link-local defaults to the REST blacklist, and 6cfa3bcca357c56e615b93462c5e70fd81b891fc adds throwIfBlacklisted to all six automation request paths. Its direct fetch still follows redirects automatically. e7d47625be8b0e3d030a5ca5d1fd604f25098efe replaces those calls with fetchWithBlacklist, uses redirect:`manual`, and calls throwIfBlacklisted(nextUrl) before every hop, closing the remaining redirect SSRF; both 62f50d9 and 6cfa3bc are ancestors of e7d47625. Tag 3.34.1 resolves to da6b1c1d6f35d78d70a1e8cf21c8b41e92931161 and `git grep` shows all six automation files still calling fetch(url) directly. Tag 3.34.2 resolves to 5533f6c3273abdc31afb28b75594327c9a87af35 and contains e7d47625 plus fetchWithBlacklist calls in all six files; it is the first tag containing e7d47625. Thus repository history places the complete automation fix boundary at 3.34.2 (the REST default component first appears in tag 3.33.4), earlier than the advisory metadata's conservative `< 3.41.3` / first-patched 3.41.3 declaration. Tags 3.41.2 and 3.41.3 both contain e7d47625, and their delta has no blacklist or automation-step fix, confirming 3.41.3 is not the actual first containing tag.
reasoning: The security invariant is that every server-originated request to an automation-controlled destination, including redirects, must reject internal and configured-blacklist addresses by default. The earliest causal violation is the original outgoing-webhook action in 3ae82b95: its parent cannot make that automation request, while the commit creates the user-controlled server-side request without a guard. The axios-to-node-fetch change and later action implementations preserve or duplicate the vulnerability rather than originate it. The March 2026 patch chain first makes the REST policy safe by default, then applies it to automation actions, then closes the redirect bypass; e7d47625 is the last direct code commit needed for the advisory's described attack path. Because the BIC commit object contains only a normal human author/committer identity and no qualifying AI attribution, the vulnerability is NOT_AI regardless of any AI activity elsewhere in repository history.
